what: The processing state of every source the book draws on, authored by the librarian. A source's default state comes from where it is: a newsroom article from its survey class (bring: to-process; content: to-mine; context: background; skip: skipped), a site article or a decision: to-process, a 2018 file: from the map (answered or unanswered). This file overrides the default where the librarian has done the work: 'processed' means its ideas are in the ideas register (ideas.json names it as a source); 'mined' means a content article's number, story or quote has been attached to an idea. The build refuses a 'processed' source that no idea cites.

states.to-process: a source the book should bring; its ideas not yet extracted
states.processed: its ideas are in the register
states.to-mine: has an example, number, story or quote to take; not yet attached to an idea
states.background: context for the agents, not for the reader
states.placed: every idea from it has a destination decided by Dinis

rule: A newsroom 'bring' article becomes 'processed' automatically when an idea cites it; a 'content' article becomes 'mined' the same way. The librarian adds an override only to say something the citations cannot: that an article was read and has nothing more to give (background), or that Dinis has placed everything from it (placed).
